ops.body:
EINTR hypothesis REFUTED on darwin, real cause found and fixed (worktree agent-aa4462b6b27b066d5).

Discriminator evidence:
1. Captured stderr from a real failing pytest run (assert patched to stop discarding it; failed on iteration 12/25): the replacement died with "codex-ask: lane ... busy; --await it or mint a new lane" — the busy refusal the narrowing had ruled unreachable, NOT "cannot acquire lane lock". So the exclusive lock was granted to the replacement while generation 1 was still in flight.
2. C probe on this host: Darwin flock(2) does return EINTR with a no-SA_RESTART handler, but the kernel transparently restarts it under SA_RESTART — and Go installs every handler (SIGURG included) with SA_RESTART. 300 external SIGURGs against a codex-ask blocked on a contended flock: survived, completed rc=0 after release. flock EINTR cannot occur in this binary on darwin.

Root cause: askMode's laneLock (*os.File) is unreferenced on the foreground path after the --dispatch branch; Go's os.File finalizer closes the fd when the value becomes unreachable, and the close releases the flock mid-run. The replacement then acquires EX, sees status empty + worker alive, and dies "lane busy" (inside the 0.5s poll window → the originally captured "escaped the foreground lock" assert; later → rc!=0 at communicate). GC timing explains the flake rate and why the standalone Python repro (different allocation profile) never fired. GOGC=1 made it 10/10 reproducible pre-fix.

Fix: defer releaseLaneLock(laneLock) in askMode (never runs — every path os.Exit — but anchors the File against the finalizer; same pattern awaitMode already had), explicit release in the --dispatch branch dropped (process exit releases it identically). Verified: GOGC=1 repro 0/10 post-fix; new Go regression test TestForegroundLaneLockSurvivesGC (GOGC=1, blocking stub, same-lane replacement must stay blocked); full go test -race green; pytest golden loop in flight (20x default + 5x GOGC=1).
